evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.10.2: sine tē omnia mea mūta esse
Sen. Ep. 6.4: nūllīus bonī sine sociō jūcunda possessiō est
terms.comment: “Without any” is sine ūllō, never sine nūllō. Nōn sine is a favourite understatement: nōn sine pugillāribus, not without my notebooks.

terms.gloss: without (doing), after a negative: never … without …
terms.grammar: conjunction with the subjunctive, after a negative clause
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.95: numquam tam male est Siculīs quīn aliquid facētē et commodē dīcant
terms.comment: “Without doing” has no single Latin form: after a negative, quīn; elsewhere a participle with nōn, or a second clause with nec.

evidence: Plaut. Men. 1022: nam absque tē esset, hodiē numquam ad sōlem occāsum vīverem
terms.comment: In Plautus and Terence only in the condition absque tē esset, had it not been for you (Lewis & Short). As a plain “without” it belongs to later Latin; use sine.

phrases.latin: eī cupientī audīre nostra dīxī sine tē omnia mea mūta esse
phrases.english: when he wanted to hear my work, I told him that without you all my writing was dumb

phrases.latin: difficilis facilis, jūcundus acerbus es īdem: nec tēcum possum vīvere, nec sine tē
phrases.english: difficult and easy, sweet and sour, you are all at once: I can’t live with you, or without you

phrases.latin: sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs
phrases.english: may the night come with sleep, and the day without quarrels

phrases.latin: nūllīus bonī sine sociō jūcunda possessiō est
phrases.english: no good thing is a pleasure to have without someone to share it

phrases.latin: Hispānī sine ūllā mōle in utrēs vestīmentīs conjectīs ipsī caetrīs superpositīs incubantēs flūmen trānāvēre
phrases.english: the Spaniards, without any fuss, stuffed their clothes into leather bags, lay on their shields on top of them and swam the river

phrases.latin: numquam tam male est Siculīs quīn aliquid facētē et commodē dīcant
phrases.english: things are never so bad for the Sicilians that they don’t say something witty and apt

phrases.latin: vēnor aliquandō, sed nōn sine pugillāribus, ut quamvīs nihil cēperim nōn nihil referam
phrases.english: I hunt now and then, but not without my notebooks, so that even if I catch nothing I bring something home
